item.title: 'Didn't do for Nobel': Trump repeats tariff claim on India-Pak war; calls Gaza truce his 8th solved conflict
item.description: US President Donald Trump claimed he resolved numerous long-standing global conflicts, including India-Pakistan disputes, by leveraging economic measures like tariffs. He stated this would be his eighth war ended, referencing the Gaza ceasefire. However, India has consistently rejected US intervention, asserting the India-Pakistan ceasefire was a result of direct military talks without third-party mediation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: The Tomahawk ultimatum: Trump's warning shot to Moscow; Putin told to end war or face US wrath
item.description: US President Donald Trump has warned Russia that he might supply long-range Tomahawk missiles to Ukraine if the war isn't settled, a move that could significantly escalate pressure on Moscow. Trump conveyed this possibility after a "productive" call with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, who sought enhanced long-range capabilities. This potential escalation follows Russia's attacks on Ukraine's power grid.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘The war is over’: Donald Trump heads for Middle East to mark Gaza ceasefire; calls it ‘very special time’
item.description: US President Donald Trump embarked on a significant trip to Israel and Egypt, heralding a ceasefire and hostage release deal that he declared has ended the Gaza war. He expressed excitement for this "very special moment" and the "historic" peace efforts, anticipating a joint ceremony and chairing a Gaza peace summit with Egyptian PM al-Sisi.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: France’s political turmoil: PM Sebastien Lecornu attempts to steady Emmanuel Macron’s shaky ship, unveils new cabinet
item.description: France's Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has unveiled a new Cabinet, blending centrist, conservative, and external figures. Facing immediate challenges like budget creation and investor confidence, the government must navigate a fractured parliament. Key appointments include a new defense minister for Ukraine support and an interior minister for security, as France grapples with political turmoil and calls for new elections.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas plane crash: Massive fire erupts after multiple trucks hit near Hicks Airfield in Fort Worth
item.description: Tragedy struck near Hicks Airfield in Texas as a small plane crashed, claiming at least two lives. The aircraft impacted several trucks, igniting a significant fire that emergency crews worked to control. Investigations by the FAA and NTSB are anticipated to determine the cause of this devastating incident.

item.title: ‘Muslims, Jews, Christians all unified’: JD Vance hails Donald Trump for uniting Israel-Gulf - ‘hostages going to live their lives’
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance lauded President Trump's role in a Gaza peace deal, anticipating the imminent release of remaining hostages. Vance highlighted Trump's unconventional diplomatic approach, which he believes united Israel, Gulf Arab nations, and diverse faiths. He clarified that US troops will monitor a ceasefire, not deploy on the ground in Gaza.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas man who posted anti-India rant over Ganesh Chaturthi procession removed from church. He says he won't take back his H-1B comment
item.description: A Texas businessman's rant against H-1B cost him dearly as he has now been removed from his gym and also from his church. He deleted the controversial post in which he said H-1Bs should be canceled as he did not want his kids to be raised in India. He made the post when he saw a Hindu religious proceeding in his area. His church asked for an apology for his sin, which he refused, as he said he won't change his stand on immigration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Evening of tears, joy’: Benjamin Netanyahu accepts war mismanagement amid backlash; IDF launches Op ‘Returning Home’
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu acknowledged divisions over a Gaza ceasefire deal, urging national unity as hostages are set to return. He described the moment as a mix of sorrow for prisoner exchanges and joy for the hostages' homecoming. The IDF launched 'Operation Returning Home' after two years of pressure, emphasizing ongoing security challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

The Bad Bunny Super Bowl controversy: Why is MAGA angry?
item.description: President Trump expressed disbelief over Bad Bunny headlining the 2026 Super Bowl halftime show, unaware of the artist's global streaming success. Bad Bunny's cultural impact and advocacy for Puerto Rico have sparked backlash from some MAGA supporters, despite his significant achievements and growing popularity.

item.title: North Korea parade: Is Kim Jong Un stronger than ever?
item.description: North Korea marked its Workers' Party 80th anniversary with a massive military parade, showcasing its arsenal and bolstering ties with China and Russia. Kim Jong Un's regime, strengthened by global rivalries and support for Russia's Ukraine war, seeks nuclear power recognition. This event highlights Kim's consolidation of power and evolving military doctrine.

item.title: What happens during a US government shutdown?
item.description: A US government shutdown began October 1st as Congress and the President failed to agree on a budget, leading to federal employee layoffs. This shutdown, rooted in disputes over healthcare policy, particularly the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid, has already impacted federal workers and public services. The duration remains uncertain as both parties remain entrenched in their positions.

item.title: Madagascar: Elite army unit turns on President Rajoelina
item.description: Madagascar's influential CAPSAT military unit has declared control over the nation's armed forces amidst escalating anti-government protests. President Rajoelina alleges an illegal power grab. The CAPSAT unit, which previously supported Rajoelina's rise in 2009, has now joined demonstrators demanding political change, following clashes with police and a rising death toll.

item.title: US CDC layoff: Hundreds reinstated as ‘incorrect notification’ fired them, after Donadl Trump’s vow to ‘fire Democrats-aligned workers’
item.description: Hundreds of CDC employees mistakenly laid off have been reinstated after an "incorrect notification" error. While many "disease detectives" and public health personnel are back, some from specific offices and violence prevention programs remain separated as part of a broader federal workforce reduction. President Trump indicated plans to dismiss many federal workers he deemed "Democrat-oriented."
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘This is vile’: Man exposes himself and urinates on altar in St Peter’s Basilica, leaves visitors ‘absolutely shocked, disgusted’
item.description: Shocking scenes unfolded at St. Peter's Basilica as a man urinated on the sacred Altar of Confession during Holy Mass. Hundreds of worshippers witnessed the deeply disrespectful act, leaving them horrified. Security intervened, but the incident has reignited concerns about security at the Vatican's most revered site, which has seen similar breaches recently.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What the 'One Piece' pirate flag means in Gen Z protests
item.description: The "One Piece" Jolly Roger, a symbol of freedom and resistance, has become a rallying cry for global Gen Z protests. Originating from a popular manga series, the flag represents challenging corrupt powers and fighting for individual choice. Its adoption by youth movements in Indonesia, Nepal, and beyond highlights its power as a unifying pop culture symbol of discontent.
